labeling_rules: member = a founder, co-founder or startup-side person writing about their own company's 83(b), 409A, incorporation or cap table, or advising peers from startup-side experience in a room forum (Hacker News, Quora, Indie Hackers, Reddit, Avvo/JustAnswer/TurboTax questions in the first person).
Startup employees writing about their own option grants, job offers, strike prices or early exercise (Blind, 'after joining a startup') are labeled other: they are a neighbouring room, not founders.
seller = a page by a company or firm that sells a fix (409A providers, cap-table software, incorporation and 83(b) filing services, law and accounting firms, their help centres and videos).
media = independent review and comparison sites, aggregator listing pages (G2, Capterra, Trustpilot), news, associations, VC blogs and newsletters about the room.
other = official pages (IRS, Delaware, SEC), job boards, contract-clause databases, unrelated or junk titles, and employee posts.
money = the text names a price, cost, fee, amount, tax owed or currency. failed_spend = the writer says they paid for something (a service, a lawyer) that did not solve the problem.
Pain keys are given when the text names the problem; a title that only names a product, site or topic gets no pain.

pains.label: I missed the 30-day 83(b) deadline. What now, and what do I owe?
pains.definition: The writer or their co-founders did not file the 83(b) within 30 days of the stock grant, or learned about it too late (nobody told them), and asks about fixes (late filing, cancelling and reissuing the grant) and the tax bill at each vesting date.

pains.label: I mailed my 83(b) but can't prove the IRS got it.
pains.definition: The election was sent but there is no confirmation: lost in the mail, lost certified-mail receipt or stamped copy, the IRS says it can't find it, or no reply after months. The writer asks how to prove it was filed on time.

pains.label: I'm a non-US founder with no SSN. How do I file the 83(b)?
pains.definition: A foreign founder (no SSN, ITIN pending, living abroad, foreign entity) asks whether the 83(b) applies to them and how to file it, including confusing or wrong guidance from the incorporation service.

pains.label: How do I fill in and file the 83(b) correctly (address, values, which shares, online form)?
pains.definition: Mechanics questions: whether the election applies to their grant (LLC, S-corp, options, reverse vesting, part of a grant), where to mail it, what amount to write, how to use the new online Form 15620, which filing tool to use, and how to fix or revoke a wrongly filed form.

pains.label: How do I report the 83(b) on my tax return?
pains.definition: After filing, the writer asks how to show the election on the return (no salary or W-2, which tax year, forgot to attach a copy) and whether tax software handles it.

pains.label: The service I paid for got my 83(b) wrong.
pains.definition: Stripe Atlas, Carta, Clerky, a lawyer or another paid service gave wrong information about the 83(b), auto-filed it wrongly, or never told the founder about it, and the writer now has to fix it.

pains.label: A 409A costs too much for us. Where do I get a cheap or free one?
pains.definition: The startup needs a 409A to grant options but the quoted price (even Carta's) is too high for its stage; the writer looks for the cheapest, free or do-it-yourself route and asks what a fair price is.

pains.label: Do I need a 409A at all, and when (pre-seed, bootstrapped, after a SAFE, how often)?
pains.definition: The writer is unsure whether their company needs a 409A yet, whether a SAFE or a priced round forces a new one, and how often it must be refreshed.

pains.label: The 409A came out too high (or looks wrong) and sets my strike price.
pains.definition: The valuation or the strike price it sets seems too high or inconsistent (above the last round, below the negotiated price, an auditor or the IRS may not accept it); the writer wants to challenge the draft or get a lower, defensible number.

pains.label: We granted options without a valid 409A. What are the penalties?
pains.definition: Options were granted with no 409A, an expired one, or one that lost safe harbour; the writer fears IRS penalties for the employees and the company and asks how to fix it.

pains.label: Which 409A provider can I trust for safe harbour: Carta, a cheap online firm, or a boutique?
pains.definition: The writer compares providers on price, speed, audit defence and whether the IRS and auditors accept the report, and asks whether a cheap or bundled 409A is legit.

pains.label: Carta costs too much, raised prices or is hard to cancel; I want a cheaper cap-table tool.
pains.definition: Complaints about cap-table software: price increases, hidden costs, cancellation trouble, unwanted outreach to investors, and the search for a cheaper or open-source alternative (Pulley, Eqvista, Cake, Ledgy, AngelList, LTSE).

pains.label: I regret paying Stripe Atlas / Clerky / doola / Firstbase; wrong fit or poor service.
pains.definition: The writer paid an incorporation service and found it a bad fit (foreign entity, online business, non-US resident), got poor support or wrong advice, or asks whether the fee is worth it.

pains.label: The Delaware franchise tax bill is a shock or overpaid, and Form 3921 must be filed on time.
pains.definition: Yearly Delaware franchise tax and annual report (March 1), picking the calculation method to avoid overpaying, and the Form 3921 filing for employee ISO exercises.
